Marta: heads-up — noticed a perf regression after yesterday's kernel-selector tweak when serving Mixtral drafts paired with Mistral runtime variants. p99 jumped on low-latency paths.
Zheng: saw that too. dug into traces, root cause looks like increased KV cache misses + a different kernel chosen for cross-family attention -> more kernel-switch overhead. short dump below.
Zheng: ```
$ ./runtime-profiler --trace request_id=abc123 --model=mixtral-draft --variant=mistral-opt
batch_size=1 seq=128 kernel=attn_fused_v2 switch_ms=4.2 kv_hit=false total_ms=48.7
batch_size=1 seq=128 kernel=attn_fused_v1 switch_ms=0.9 kv_hit=true total_ms=34.1
```
Tim: kv_hit=false for drafts is suspicious. Are we invalidating KV on handshake due to RoPE/dimension mismatch? I remember code that forces KV flush if family mismatch > 0.1 in head dims. :thinking:
Katelyn: tokenizer mismatch also visible in acceptance logs — the draft pairing is sometimes selecting mixtral-draft -> mistral-opt but tokenization differences drop acceptance rate from ~0.78 to ~0.62 on our eval set. acceptance tuning we pushed last month didn't account for this family cross-variance.
Dave: quick numbers from the canary (10%): baseline p99=34ms, canary p99=49ms. p95 went from 18ms -> 22ms. CPU on the host didn't spike, GPU utilization slightly lower (less efficient kernels).
deploy-bot: canary rollout at 10% started by @Marta (id 0x7f) — monitors: latency, errors, acceptance_rate.
Marta: my hypothesis: kernel-selector heuristic currently favors a unified kernel for <seq=256 but when pairing models across families it picks the 'safe' kernel which has worse throughput for our actual head/kv dims. Also KV cache invalidation policy may be too aggressive when rope_scale differs between model families.
Zheng: validated: when rope_scale diff > 1.02 we set KV.force_invalidate(true). Example: mixtral draft rope_scale=1.0 vs mistral-opt=0.985 -> triggers invalidation. that threshold is too tight.
Tim: proposal: make rope_scale threshold adaptive by model pair and consider head_dim alignment rather than scalar rope_scale only. fallback: keep KV if head_dim == head_dim and kv_dim_ratio within 3%.
Katelyn: on acceptance side, immediate mitigation: add tokenizer-normalization layer on pairing path that maps tokens between close families (fixes whitespace/byte-level diffs). short-term param: acceptance_threshold -= 0.05 for cross-family pairing (helps recall but watch hallucination).
Dave: also try forcing kernel v1 for these pairings and measure throughput — should lower latency variance until we have a better selector.
Zheng: ran microbench: forcing attn_fused_v1 -> p99 35.2ms, attn_fused_v2 -> p99 48.9ms on the described pairing with seq=128 bs=1. KV.keep improves p99 by ~9ms on median.
Marta: action items: 1) revert kernel-selector change for mixed-family pairing (timed flag). 2) relax rope_scale invalidation threshold to 1.05 and add head_dim check. 3) add tokenizer normalization step for pairing path. 4) run 24h canary with acceptance and p99 gates.
Zheng: I'll open a PR with the threshold change + unit tests for head_dim logic.
Tim: I'll prototype an adaptive batching heuristic: per-model max_batch_tokens = min(global, model_pref * 0.9) when speculative decoding on — aim to reduce tail latency from batching-induced head-of-queue waits.
Katelyn: I'll patch the pairing service with normalization shim and add eval harness to measure acceptance/regression with our 10k prompt set.
Dave: set canary rollback guard: if p99 increases > 15ms or acceptance drops > 6 percentage points within 6h, auto revert.
Marta: good. please tag tickets and timestamp experiments. prefer not to ship to Dedicated customers until we confirm no regression.
Zheng: FYI logs and perf snapshots uploaded to /mnt/profiler/1987654321/ — link: https://internal.redwood/profiler/1987654321
Marta: thanks — syncing with product on potential customer impact. anyone see additional signals (cost, token throughput) post-canary?
Dave: cost per token slightly up for canary (~3% for these flows) due to inefficient kernel. tracking.
Tim: fine to run experiments in parallel: kernel-selector rollback + tokenizer shim + batching tweak. we can A/B each.
Katelyn: will add acceptance slices by prompt family so we can see regressions localized to code/docs chatty prompts.
Marta: nailed. I'll own the rollout and verification. ping me for access to canary dashboards. :thumbsup:
deploy-bot: canary updated: watchers notified.
Marta: closing loop — if no surprises in 24h we can bake changes into next release.
